title: Letter from Wilhelmina Drucker to Aletta Jacobs regarding Suffrage
excerpt: This personal correspondence from 1899 discusses strategies for the women's suffrage movement. Drucker emphasizes the necessity of public demonstrations over quiet political lobbying, arguing that 'the vote will not be given, it must be taken.' The letter is dated October 12th and references a scheduled meeting in The Hague.
full_text: Dearest Aletta, I write to you today with urgency. The current pace of the suffrage movement is too slow. We must escalate. The vote will not be given, it must be taken. Let's organize a large public march in The Hague next month to demonstrate our numbers and resolve.
creator: Wilhelmina Drucker
